is_anopheles.evidence: The study analyzes Anopheles gambiae, Anopheles funestus, Anopheles coluzzii, and other Anopheles species (Abstract, Table 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-w) mutation (Abstract, Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts for the L1014F mutation are provided on page 7: 'Thus 92.3 % of the An. gambiae sister taxa mosquitoes presented a homozygous resistant profile of the type RR (n = 169), 4.4 % a heterozygous profile RS (n = 8)... None of the tested An. gambiae sister taxa mosquitoes was found to be homozygous for the insecticide sensitive wild type kdr allele L1014.'

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from 15 districts in Bangui, Central African Republic (Abstract, Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study describing original entomological and genetic data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to 15 specific districts in Bangui, such as Gbanikola, Taoka Saint Paul, and PK 10 (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted in 2013 (September–October and November–December) (Abstract).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study appears to be an independent collection by the Institut Pasteur and does not mention being part of a larger surveillance network or consortium.

supplement.evidence: Additional file 5: Table S1 contains molecular attribute data (genotypes) for mosquitoes collected in 4 districts of Bangui, which would provide finer spatial resolution than the aggregate counts in the text.

assessment.summary: The study characterizes the composition and insecticide resistance genetics of Anopheles populations in Bangui, Central African Republic, in 2013. It reports high frequencies of the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-w) mutation in the Anopheles gambiae complex, with the resistant allele nearly fixed (92.3% RR, 4.4% RS, 0% SS).
